executive_summary:
Del Taco is a Yadav Enterprises-owned, predominantly franchised Mexican QSR executing an 18-month post-acquisition turnaround called Project Sunrise. At fiscal year-end September 28, 2025, the inherited estate comprised 576 restaurants—132 company-operated and 444 franchised—with $918.8 million in systemwide sales. The operating baseline was pressured: system same-store sales declined 3.7%, company-store transactions declined 6.9%, and restaurant-level margin was 11.1%.

Yadav's leadership reset and Project Sunrise create an active transformation agenda centered on unit-level execution, cost optimization, consistent food quality, value, guest trust, and modernization of systems and processes. Nick Hulayew reported on September 8 that Del Taco is reviewing the full technology stack, including payments, digital menu boards, POS hardware, and POS software. This expands the potential motion beyond a DMB-only wedge, although scope, timing, budget, and decision authority still require direct confirmation.

Worldpay's contract extension was signed September 3, 2026 after an approximately nine-month process. Maggie Lenhart owns the Worldpay relationship, Todd Vahlsing owns the Genius expansion motion, and Nick has a separate relationship path through Daniel Mears, a reported Del Taco IT director whom Nick invited to Genius World. Nick agreed to reconnect with Daniel and introduce Todd. Dean, reported by Nick as Yadav's CTO and a Genius advisory-board member, is described as a strong Genius champion, but his actual decision authority requires validation.

The recommended posture is relationship-led and discovery-first. Coordinate Maggie's Worldpay access with Nick's Daniel Mears relationship, qualify the comprehensive review, and position hardware reuse as a capital-efficient differentiator. Treat the reported Anil Yadav–Qu investment relationship as an unconfirmed competitive risk, not an established fact.
current_business_situation:
Del Taco entered Yadav Enterprises ownership on December 22, 2025 following a sale by Jack in the Box valued at approximately $119 million after customary adjustments. The inherited operating base comprised 576 restaurants at fiscal year-end 2025, with 444 franchised and 132 company-operated locations. Fiscal 2025 systemwide sales were $918.8 million, while system same-store sales declined 3.7%, company-store transactions declined 6.9%, and restaurant-level margin was 11.1%. Fourteen restaurants opened while 32 closed.

Management is executing Project Sunrise, an 18-month turnaround centered on restoring core food quality and consistency, simplifying operations, strengthening value, rebuilding guest trust, accelerating executable menu innovation, expanding catering, and improving loyalty.

Nick Hulayew reported on September 8 that Del Taco is conducting a comprehensive review spanning payments, digital menu boards, POS hardware, and POS software. Nick previously invited Daniel Mears to Genius World and met him there; he agreed to reconnect with Daniel and introduce Todd. The exact review stage, governance, budget, requirements, and timetable remain unconfirmed.

Internal account history captured September 8 indicates that Del Taco previously evaluated Genius for digital menu boards while under Jack in the Box ownership. The latest historical concept was a stopgap configuration retaining static boards with an approximately 32-inch screen in the center. Technical discussions occurred, but the desired system-on-chip approach did not align cleanly with the Genius solution at that time and the initiative went quiet around the divestiture. This is historical context, not evidence that the same requirement remains active.

The signed Worldpay extension removes the renewal-period coordination constraint and creates a cleaner window for joint discovery. Together, Maggie's Worldpay relationship and Nick's access to Daniel create two coordinated routes into the account, but neither substitutes for direct qualification with current Yadav and Del Taco decision-makers.
